comparison.objective: Punch a wire into a 110 termination block with the punch-down tool’s cutting side oriented toward the loose end; unlike commissioning and locking an adjustable shock absorber through repeated carriage-cycle evaluation.
comparison.physical_skill: Requires positioning a wire, orienting and aligning a punch-down tool with a 110-block slot, then applying an insertion/cutting stroke. The candidate instead requires recessed hex-key engagement, bimanual counterholding, setscrew unlocking/relocking, fine collar rotation, bounded tightening, and iterative dynamic-response adjustment.
comparison.success_condition: Available evidence only states successful wire punch-down with the cutting side facing the loose end; it supplies no rubric, numeric threshold, damage rule, or spec version. Even with those details missing, this outcome is meaningfully different from two repeatable energy-bounded carriage stops without bottoming, hard-stop contact, overload, excessive rebound, or collar drift after physical relocking.
comparison.reason: The complete indexed record contains an empty body and no spec versions, so comparison is limited to its title. That title nevertheless establishes a different tested objective, manipulation mechanism, and outcome: wire termination and trimming in a 110 block versus adjustment, locking, and dynamic validation of an industrial damper. Shared tool alignment and force application are only generic primitives and do not establish overlap.
